title: Lonely Pixel I
description:
Given an m x n picture consisting of black 'B' and white 'W' pixels, return the number of black lonely pixels.
A black lonely pixel is a character 'B' that located at a specific position where the same row and same column don't have any other black pixels.
 
Example 1:


Input: picture = [["W","W","B"],["W","B","W"],["B","W","W"]]
Output: 3
Explanation: All the three 'B's are black lonely pixels.

Example 2:


Input: picture = [["B","B","B"],["B","B","W"],["B","B","B"]]
Output: 0

 
Constraints:

m == picture.length
n == picture[i].length
1 <= m, n <= 500
picture[i][j] is 'W' or 'B'.

def check(candidate):
    assert candidate(picture=[['W', 'W', 'B'], ['W', 'B', 'W'], ['B', 'W', 'W']]) == 3
    assert candidate(picture=[['B', 'B', 'B'], ['B', 'B', 'W'], ['B', 'B', 'B']]) == 0
    assert candidate(picture=[['B']]) == 1
    assert candidate(picture=[['W']]) == 0
    assert candidate(picture=[['B', 'W'], ['W', 'W']]) == 1
    assert candidate(picture=[['W', 'B', 'W', 'W'], ['W', 'W', 'W', 'W'], ['B', 'W', 'W', 'W'], ['W', 'W', 'W', 'B']]) == 3
    assert candidate(picture=[['B', 'W', 'B'], ['W', 'W', 'W'], ['B', 'W', 'B']]) == 0
    assert candidate(picture=[['W', 'W', 'W'], ['W', 'B', 'W'], ['W', 'W', 'W']]) == 1
